messages:
maya: Heads-up — last hour saw steady queue growth on us-east primary for customer-tier=pro. We hit sustained slot saturation, and a few requests were dropped with 429/503.
sandeep: Ugh. Is this the same autoscale gap we saw last quarter or a different pattern? Any metrics on latency vs queue? 
maya: It's capacity-bound not latency. backend GPU slots full; queue backlog rises. We have a working RFC for automatic variant fallback but need ops + API contract decisions.
jon: From a UX/contract pov we need an explicit opt-in per-tenant + an API signal for sticky vs best-effort fallback. Otherwise users will get surprising model fidelity changes.
liz: Agreed. Suggestion: default behavior = no auto-fallback for new tenants, console toggle under Model Routing -> "Auto variant failover (capacity)". Admins can enable per-tenant.
kevin: For API, propose header `X-RW-Fallback: enabled;mode=best-effort;sticky=false` and also support `mode=preserve-quality` which only falls back to compatible variants (same arch / tokenizer).
maya: +1 for header. Also need a route-level config in the control plane so customers can pin models with a fallback policy. Console should show when a request was served by fallback (to make it debuggable).
jon: Telemetry: emit `fallback.triggered` with tags {tenant, primary_model, fallback_model, reason=saturation, slot_usage_pct}. Console should surface count and a sample of prompts where quality regressed.
sandeep: Ops concerns: we must avoid oscillation. Implement a short cool-down per-tenant + sticky session for N minutes after a fallback, unless tenant explicitly opted for non-sticky via header.
kevin: Implementation note: fallback candidates should be validated at deploy-time for compatibility (vocab, input shape). If incompatible, return `422` with friendly message instead of silent fallback.
liz: Rollout plan: Stage 1 = feature flag for internal tenants only; Stage 2 = console toggle + docs; Stage 3 = public opt-in; Stage 4 = safe default for low-tier (opt-out for high-tier). We should add a canary: start with 1% of pro tenants.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy: auto-fallback-service v0.3 -> 1% traffic (group=internal) at 2026-03-18T15:10Z
maya: QA checklist: load test with synthetic hot tenants, verify logs contain `fallback.triggered`, validate no tenant sees >2 sequential model switches within 10m, validate billing attribution unchanged but note cost delta.
jon: Console telemetry UX: show a small "fallback burst" banner on route details with a link to session-level traces. Also expose an API `GET /v1/tenants/:id/fallbacks` to fetch history.
sandeep: One more: graceful degrade ordering — prefer lower-precision variant (quantized) of same model before swapping architecture. That keeps semantics closest.
kevin: Agree. Add preference hierarchy: same-model-quantized -> same-arch-smaller -> compatible-arch -> last-resort-generic. Document it.
maya: OK let's capture decisions and I'll draft the PR: API header + control-plane config + console toggle + telemetry events + cooldown sticky logic + candidate-validation. I'll include the canary rollout plan.
liz: Thanks — ping once PR is up, we'll add a tiny section in the console help and email RB to SEs. :thumbsup:
